fixes.explanation: Angry isn't Peter's word, baker. I think a long wait can sound like a short fuse to a scoffer, but Peter says the Lord “…is patient with you…” And that “you” is the very people he keeps calling beloved. Patience is the word he picks, and it's a long way from anger.

Offerings aren't in this verse, friend. Peter says the Lord is “…not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.” Nothing in that sentence asks anyone to bring something. It's about people, and where they end up (2 Peter 3:9).

Silence does sound peaceful, baker, but Peter doesn't go there. He says “…where righteousness dwells.” After all that fire and melting, he doesn't promise a quiet place. He promises a place where righteousness has a home (2 Peter 3:13).

Doubt isn't where Peter lands, baker. He says, “Consider also that our Lord’s patience brings salvation…” The scoffers ask where the promise is, but Peter asks believers to look at the waiting again and see salvation in it. Doubt only sees the clock.
